headline: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank’s first visible pressure point is asset quality, not a confirmed funding event
dek: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is the sole orange institution in the current monitored set, but the designation rests on an aged filing-period signal: GNPA of 9.4%. Market confirmation is unavailable for publication, and key funding lenses are dark.

headline: Rupee Co-operative Bank replay: the signal was an evidence boundary, not a clean warning
dek: This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. Rupee Co-operative Bank’s record shows why a balance-sheet screen must separate a filing-period signal, a market-price signal, and an absence of scoreable evidence.

headline: Before the event: what Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank's filings did and did not reveal
dek: A construction-PIT replay of Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank: the first published regulatory or funding signal, the disclosure clock, the miss, and the boundary that survives into today's screen.

headline: Religare Finvest’s funding signal was early—not a clean prediction of failure
dek: A historical replay places a Watch-band funding reading before Religare Finvest’s default. The narrower lesson is that liability strain can reveal vulnerability before formal thresholds do, while fraud can make disclosure-based screens falsely reassuring.

headline: IL&FS replay: the funding signal arrived before the threshold lenses named a break
dek: IL&FS’s disclosed funding lens reached watch well before default, while the public action-zone replay recorded no first entry. That sequence is a historical prompt for diligence, not proof of foresight or a forecast.

headline: Global Trust Bank’s warning appeared before the event—but its limits matter as much as its lead
dek: The replay shows reported capital and asset-quality breaches before Global Trust Bank’s default, while an unscoreable funding lens and a fraud-masked record make the case for escalation, not prediction.

headline: Altico’s replay points to rollover funding before an action-zone signal
dek: Altico’s disclosed commercial-paper reliance was a liability-side vulnerability in the historical record. The finding is a filing-period signal, not a market-price call or a model-derived failure forecast.

headline: Abhyudaya’s earliest disclosed warning was an asset-quality tripwire
dek: This historical replay finds that Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank entered an RBI action zone on NNPA in FY2021, well before its event date. It is a disclosure-timed signal, not a forecast, a market-price verdict, or a calibrated probability of failure.

headline: Sambandh Finserve’s funding flag arrived early—but did not make failure knowable
dek: A fragile wholesale-leverage reading preceded Sambandh Finserve’s recorded default. It was a filing-period vulnerability signal, not a market-price verdict, calibrated failure probability, or forecast for institutions on today’s board.

headline: Before the event: what New India Co-operative Bank's filings did and did not reveal
dek: A construction-PIT replay of New India Co-operative Bank: the first published regulatory or funding signal, the disclosure clock, the miss, and the boundary that survives into today's screen.

headline: Nedungadi Bank’s capital breach preceded the event. The harder question is what that warning could—and could not—establish.
dek: The replay records an RBI action-zone CRAR breach for Nedungadi Bank at FY1999, before its default. It is evidence of an early disclosed constraint under a proxy clock, not proof of a tradable forecast or a complete account of the institution’s failure.

headline: United Western Bank’s earliest recorded warning was a filing signal, not a market call
dek: The historical replay records an NNPA action-zone breach before United Western Bank’s default. That is evidence of a disclosed rule breach at a filing period, not proof of causation, a contemporaneous market-price warning, or a calibrated forecast.

headline: Utkarsh is the orange balance-sheet watch, but the evidence is aging
dek: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is the sole orange name on the current LiquiLens Failure Radar. That status rests on an old filing-period asset-quality signal, not on a market verdict, a funding event, or a prediction of failure.

headline: ESAF’s stress signal is not funding flight. It is a narrowing margin for error.
dek: ESAF Small Finance Bank is a yellow-screen priority because an asset-quality burden and a stale market repricing signal can interact before a visible funding break. The available deposit signal is stable, while key liquidity evidence remains dark.

headline: ESAF is the clearest observable pressure chain, not a settled first-to-stress call
dek: An aged filing shows a high bad-loan burden and a stale market model reads below the yellow threshold. But deposits were rising in the reported quarter, key funding fields are dark, and an orange peer prevents any confident claim that ESAF will feel stress first.

headline: Religare Finvest replay: a funding watch came before default, but fraud limits what it can prove
dek: The historical record places a disclosed-liability warning ahead of Religare Finvest’s default. It does not show that a threshold screen detected fraud, established causation, or supplied a tradeable forecast.

headline: IL&FS replay: the funding signal arrived first, but the record cannot prove causation
dek: The IL&FS replay identifies a liability-side watch signal before default and before any recorded PCA action-zone entry. That is a filing-period result under optimistic timing assumptions, not a market-price verdict, a live backtest, or a forecast for today’s screens.

headline: Global Trust Bank replay: disclosed capital and asset-quality stress arrived first
dek: The replay places Global Trust Bank in an RBI action zone before its default date, but fraud-masking, an unscoreable funding lens, and period-end timing proxies sharply limit what that sequence can prove.

headline: ESAF’s warning is a dated filing signal meeting a live market-price signal—not evidence of a funding run
dek: ESAF Small Finance Bank is a yellow-tier monitoring case because an elevated GNPA reading sits beside a market distance-to-default below the screen threshold. The filing, price and model signals should not be treated as the same thing.
